sources_read: .qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r3/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx (Quality Checks!A15:D15; Internal Quality Checks!A15:G15 annotations: PII/credentials defined in prompts acceptable; 'If task data itself contain credential flag it. Only in toml we allow.')
evidence: Only shipped data file is environment/assets/seed_data.json (5701 bytes, pure ASCII, valid JSON; identical sha256 f69616e2e3d42c3ab858192126cde96cc5a39786f7f21c450b25c4ed6559be36 to solution/app/seed/seed_data.json). Scripted referential audit (python -I over the file) found zero problems: 5 unique accounts; 17 unique message ids across M-11/M-12/M-13; every author is an account; client authors only post in their own matter (gwen M-11/M-13, paul M-12); walled dev authors nothing in M-12; every wall entry is staff; every client field is a client account; every timer_days (7, null, 30) is in timer_options_days [null,1,7,30]; every parent (K-14->K-1, K-15->K-14, K-4->K-3, K-12->K-6, K-9->K-8) resolves within the same matter and precedes its reply; version 'at' values never post-date the message; no message after clock 2026-05-12T11:00:00Z (matches integration.md); messages are listed chronologically with no timestamp ties; every read_up_to entry targets a matter the user may see (no dev->M-12, no client cross-matter) and a message in that matter that survives the timer at import (K-3, K-16, K-4, K-8, K-9, K-12, K-6). Intentional edge fixtures are consistent with public notes rather than defects: K-1 (11 days, 7-day matter) expires at import but its reply K-14 survives -> the placeholder rule in walls-and-retention.md; K-10 at exactly 7 days expires vs K-11 one second later survives (the stated 'exactly seven days ago ... already gone' boundary); K-2/K-17 are overdue but held; K-2 held+edited exercises the transcript version rule; K-17 id out of numeric order discourages id-sorting. Synthetic/clean: names are fictional, all emails on the reserved .test TLD, no phone/address/DOB/ID numbers; no credential, token or secret in the seed (password123 appears only in /instructions/walls-and-retention.md, which the workbook annotation and SKILL.md line 66 treat as expected profile credentials). Regex scan for script|onerror|javascript:|ignore previous|password|token|secret|api key|http returned no hits. K-16 contains benign <b>/<i>/<u> tags and K-12 '*Schedule 4*' - these are deliberate fixtures for the public conversations.md formatting/escaping requirement, carry no executable or prompt-injection content. Graders do not depend on seed state (app_context.md: 'Do not assume the seed state'), so no criterion-vs-seed drift is possible here. Adversarial: a broken app cannot pass anything via this row (data-only check); a conforming app cannot be failed by the data because every reference resolves and edge cases follow stated public rules. No runtime evidence is required for this row.
notes: Note only: seed encodes 'edited' implicitly via a versions array (no explicit edited flag or edit timestamp; versions[].at equals the original sent time). This is a reasonable reading and the brief does not require an edit time, so not a defect. K-16 HTML tags are an intended escape fixture, not an injection payload.
